newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end lower after bank sector tumble.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end lower after bank sector tumble.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended the Wednesday session down, but well off their lows, as they was unable to recover completely from renewed rumours about the financial health of Nippon Credit Bank Ltd which made the bank sector drop with a thud in the morning, brokers said.
The 225-share Nikkei average finished 128.36 points or 0.70 percent lower at 18,185.97 after falling to a low of 17,901.48. Its March futures shed 160 points to land at 18,180.

"Nippon Credit shares fell below 200 yen to an all-time low which ignited a bank sector sell-off led by futures early in the morning and the sour mood continued throughout the day," said Akishige Ishikura, Dai-ichi Securities analyst.
Brokers added that there was some short-covering and bargain hunting which helped minimise losses whenever the Nikkei benchmark fell through the 18,000 threshold.

"It is very important that the Nikkei average closes above 18,000 after falling beneath that during the day, as the market is trying to find a concrete support level," said Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities general manager.
Turnover was 381 million shares against 397 million on Tuesday. Losers swamped winners 942 to 179 while 125 issues were unchanged.

Market sources said market volatility would continue as basic factors burdening investor sentiment, such as worries over the economy, had not changed. With investors sidelined, trade is in the hands of arbitrageurs after fast profits.
"Overall market direction is hard to discern and until something concrete emerges, we will be stuck on a roller-coaster," Dai-ichi's Ishikura said.

After the market closed for the noon break, Nippon Credit Bank said that it saw no cause for concern about its financial health. It also said that it would take serious note of the stock market's view of its share price.

But bank shares continued to wilt, Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd, the third most heavily traded stock with turnover of 6.96 million shares, lost 20 yen to 143. Fuji Bank Ltd lost 70 yen to 1,260 on trade of 5.42 million shares.
Nippon Credit said after the market closed that it would meet the media at 0800 GMT to deny the recent rumours.
Some brokers said trade in speculative shares was also bruised by Gajoen Kanko KK's plight.
The hotelier which failed to honour promissory notes for a second time, said late on Tuesday that it would apply for court mediation with its creditors over its liabilities.
Short-term fund supplier Nichiboshin Ltd fell 58 yen to 208 yen, making it the second-largest percentage loser.
Kimmon Manufacturing Co Ltd crumbled after Japan's anti-monopoly watchdog filed a complaint with prosecutors against it, brokers said. It shed 37 yen to 426 yen.
Due to the weak market sentiment, investors paid little attention to the yen's new four-year low against the dollar.
"If the market's mood were not so bad, export-related firms would surge but the market is too preoccupied with the weak bank sector to take much advantage of it," one broker said.
The yen sank briefly to 123 against the dollar in afternoon Tokyo before clawing back to the high-122 level.
Fujitsu Ltd climbed 10 yen to 1,200 and computer parts manufacturer TEAC Corp was up 46 yen at 610. Both were helped by the weak yen, brokers said.
On a sector basis, mining, warehouses, ship building, electric equipment and precision instruments led the gainers. Fisheries, oil, banks, gas and securities were the leading retreaters.

Other indices were lower. TOPIX shed 20.34 points or 1.48 percent to 1,355.40. Nikkei 300 fell 3.64 points, or 1.39 percent to 258.06. The second section index lost 11.02 points, or 0.63 percent to end at 1,738.05.
Second section turnover was 11.9 million shares, up from 9.97 million on the previous day.
The over-the-counter index was down 4.19 points or 0.33 percent at 1,276.15 in late afternoon Tokyo. -- Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-9052
